— Intersections, Emergency Vehicles, School Buses","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Intersections, Emergency Vehicles, School Buses

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Rectangular rapid-flashing beacons switch on by push button and usually sit at crossings with no traffic signal or at mid-block crosswalks [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
While the beacon amber lamps strobe, halt for anybody inside the crosswalk and watch for anybody about to step into it [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian hybrid beacon sleeps dark until a walker triggers it; dark lamps mean drive through carefully, a blinking lower yellow means ease off, and a steady lower yellow means get ready to halt [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Once the beacon twin upper reds glow steady, stop for the crossing pedestrians; when they start blinking, stop if you have not yet done so, then roll on carefully if the crossing stands empty [A01].
Why it matters: steady reds demand a full stop while blinking reds release you once the crossing clears.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Treat a person guided by a harnessed service dog or tapping a white or white-and-red cane as likely blind, and drive with added care to keep them safe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Where no signs or signals govern a meeting of road users, yield rules pick who waits; the law names who must yield but hands the right-of-way to nobody [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
Whoever holds the right-of-way, still do all you can to keep from hitting a pedestrian or another car [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
Bikes and cars share the same road rights and duties, yet riders crash unprotected, so drive defensively and yield to them even on occasions they should yield to you [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
Failing to yield the right-of-way ranks as the top cause of deadly traffic crashes in Iowa [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A02
After a full stop you may turn right on red unless a sign bans it, yielding as you go [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A02
Crossing a sidewalk or rolling into or out of a driveway, alley, or lot, give way to people on foot [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
Wheels may cross a sidewalk but may never travel along it [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
A left-turning driver waits for oncoming cars bound straight ahead [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A02
At an all-way stop the first car to arrive leaves first after stopping fully, and when cars arrive together the one on the right moves first [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A02
Pulling onto a road from a driveway, alley, or shoulder, yield to traffic already rolling there [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
Stop or yield for pedestrians in marked crossings and in unmarked ones alike [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A02
Give way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency rigs sounding a siren or horn or flashing red or blue [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
Spotting or hearing one approach from any side, ease to the right road edge or as close right as you can get [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A02
Caught inside an intersection or roundabout, drive through it before pulling aside; but on a median-split road with the rig across the divider, you need not stop at all [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A02
Hang back at least 500 feet behind a rig running lights and siren [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A02
With no stop sign or signal, every driver slows and enters with care, all the controlled-intersection rules still bind, and extra caution rules [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A03
Trailing a bus on a two- or three-lane road, its flashing red or amber lamps forbid passing and order readiness to stop [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A03
Once that bus halts with its stop arm swung out, stop no closer than 15 feet behind the bus and wait until the arm retracts and the bus moves again, then proceed carefully [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A03
Facing the bus as its amber lamps blink, slow to no more than 20 mph and prepare to stop [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A03
When the oncoming bus stops with its arm extended, halt ahead of it, stay put until the arm retracts, and roll on with care [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A03
Breaking the school-bus stopping law can cost you your license for up to 180 days [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A03
Trailing the bus on four-plus lanes, obey the same drill: never pass on flashing red or amber, stop behind the halted bus with its arm out keeping at least 15 feet back, and wait until the arm retracts and the bus moves [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A03
Meeting the bus across opposite lanes on a four-or-more-lane road, you may roll past without stopping even with its lamps flashing and arm out, the single lawful pass of a stopped, armed bus [A03].
Why it matters: this opposite-direction pass is the lone exception to the never-pass-an-armed-bus rule.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0020]

Misconceptions: the law assigns who must yield but grants the right-of-way to nobody; a dark hybrid beacon means proceed with care, not stop; oncoming traffic on a wide road need not stop for a bus across the lanes.

Mnemonic: first there, first through; tie goes right; left waits for straight; red and amber bus lamps mean feet off the gas.

Glossary: rectangular rapid-flashing beacon (a push-button amber strobe at unsignalized crossings); pedestrian hybrid beacon (a walker-triggered signal cycling yellow then red); all-way stop (an intersection where every approach must halt); stop arm (the swing-out bus sign that orders traffic to halt).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every intersection, emergency, and school-bus rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
